title: ARA Survey Outreach Campaign
subtitle: A 45-day, three-channel outreach campaign built to drive APS Academic Recovery Academy survey participation in underserved communities.
summary: Bivines Group designed and executed a 45-day, three-channel outreach campaign for Atlanta Public Schools' Academic Recovery Academy survey effort, using school-site activations, door-to-door canvassing, and a digital contest platform under an independent brand to reach families traditional district communications were missing. The campaign targeted 3,000 submissions from more than 11,000 invited households, reached an estimated 76% of the targeted population, and produced 900+ confirmed survey responses while surfacing useful operational insight about address quality, timing, and cluster performance.

carousel.title: 1. Overview
carousel.heading: A community-trust campaign disguised as a survey push
carousel.content:
ARA Survey Outreach Campaign | Atlanta, Georgia

Atlanta Public Schools needed feedback from 11,000+ families in underserved communities to evaluate a district-wide summer learning recovery program - and traditional outreach had never reached them. We designed and executed a 45-day, three-channel campaign: on-site school visits, door-to-door canvassing, and a digital contest platform built under an independent brand. We reached an estimated 76% of the targeted population and generated 900+ survey submissions.

carousel.title: 2. Details
carousel.heading: 11,000+ invited households, 24 school sites, 3 campaign channels
carousel.content:
- Client type: Urban public school district (K-12), Atlanta, GA
- Campaign duration: 45 days, June-August 2023
- Target population: 11,000+ ARA-invited households; 6,100+ enrolled students
- Submission goal: 3,000 surveys; result: 900+ confirmed (18% return rate)
- Collateral produced: 8,400 printed pieces (5,600 postcards + 2,800 door flyers)
- Doors canvassed: 2,137 projected; 1,802 connected; 769 live engagements
- Status: Completed; final report delivered August 2023

carousel.title: 3. The Situation
carousel.heading: Traditional outreach was missing the families APS most needed to hear from
carousel.content:
Atlanta Public Schools' Academic Recovery Academy was a direct response to COVID-19 learning loss - a full-day summer intervention for elementary and middle school students. APS needed to survey participating families to understand whether it was working. The families they most needed to hear from were the least likely to respond.

Research confirmed four distinct barriers driving non-response: gaps in motivation, reach, cultural fit, and perceived value. Standard district communications - email blasts, automated calls, flyers sent home - had already failed to close them. We had 45 days, a fixed address list, and a mandate to reach a population that had learned not to answer the door.

carousel.title: 4. The Ask
carousel.heading: Design an outreach system that could bridge four distinct engagement gaps
carousel.content:
The client needed survey completions. What the work actually required:

- Market segmentation distinguishing four non-response types - each requiring a different intervention
- An independent brand to house an incentive program and keep the district clear of prize liability
- Physical field operations at school sites and individual households, not just digital outreach
- A digital infrastructure - contest website, segmented intake forms, CRM automation
- Pre-built measurement tracking every door by date, time, cluster, and outcome type
- An honest final report against pre-set goals, including what didn't work

carousel.title: 5. The Approach
carousel.heading: Use an independent initiative and run three channels at once
carousel.content:
We started with a market gap analysis, not a channel plan. Before choosing tactics, we needed to know why this population doesn't respond. The answer wasn't one thing: motivation, reach, culture, and trust required four distinct interventions.

The decision to house the incentive program under an independent brand - OpinionatED Minds - was a strategic call, not a branding exercise. It gave the campaign cultural flexibility the district couldn't project on its own and shielded APS from prize liability.

We built the measurement framework before the first door was knocked. Seven status categories tracked every canvassing contact - not because we expected everything to work, but because we needed to know what to adjust in real time and what to report honestly at the end.

carousel.title: 6. The Work
carousel.heading: Field operations, collateral, digital workflows, and reporting
carousel.content:
Campaign Strategy
Full strategy document: market sizing (18,000 households represented), four-segment gap analysis, two-pronged campaign theory, and a phased 45-day milestone timeline. Focused resources on the reachable segments; named the unreachable ones explicitly.

Brand + Creative
Developed the OpinionatED Minds contest brand, website, and all collateral. Built segmented digital intake forms capturing parent verification, ARA enrollment confirmation, school site, and grade. Produced 8,400 printed pieces across two formats.

School-Site Activation
Mascot-and-ambassador teams deployed to 15 ARA sites over four days. Engaged 184 parents and 1,040+ students; distributed 905 postcards. 100% inquiry rate on mascot tactic.

Door-to-Door Operations
10-day canvass across 10 geographic clusters using an APS-provided address list. Best engagement window: 4-6 PM. Highest-performing cluster: South Atlanta at 94.22% target rate.

Digital + CRM
CRM workflow triggered automated follow-up on survey completion. 121 digital contest entries cross-referenced against ARA enrollment by cluster and grade.

carousel.title: 7. The Impact
carousel.heading: 900+ submissions, 76% saturation, and useful operational intelligence
carousel.content:
We reached an estimated 76% of the targeted ARA household population, exceeding the 75% goal set in the strategy plan.

- 900+ survey submissions confirmed at report date; 18% return rate on 6,100+ enrolled students
- 1,802 doors connected (93% of 2,137 targeted); 769 live household engagements
- 138 surveys completed at the door during canvassing operations
- 15 school sites visited in four days; 1,040+ students and 184 parents reached on-site
- Positive reception confirmed across administrators, staff, parents, and students - cited as a district priority metric
- Data quality finding: 12-18% of APS-provided addresses were vacant or non-APS households - surfaced as a district data issue with implications beyond this campaign

Submission figures represent confirmed receipts at time of final report. Campaign may have continued receiving responses after the reporting date.

carousel.title: 8. The Deliverables
carousel.heading: A full outreach stack with measurable field execution
carousel.content:
Comprehensive Campaign Strategy - 20-page brief covering gap analysis, campaign theory, channel plan, and milestone calendar

OpinionatED Minds Brand - Independent contest identity structured to operate at arm's length from the district

Contest Website - Multi-section platform with segmented intake forms, parent verification flow, and prize information

Printed Collateral Suite - 8,400 pieces across two formats: school postcard and door-to-door flyer

CRM Automation Workflow - Triggered email sequence on survey completion with full enrollment history tracking

School-Site Activation - Four-day mascot-and-ambassador deployment across 15 sites with per-site tracking

Door-to-Door Field Operation - 10-day canvass across 10 clusters, tracked at the individual-door level by status, time, and geography

Final Campaign Report - 24-page performance report with channel data, engagement funnels, cluster-level tables, and three-metric self-assessment scorecard
